## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design an end-to-end runtime security gate in a large-scale, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment, integrating policy (OPA Gatekeeper) with runtime detection (Falco) and CI validation.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA policies
- Falco runtime detection
- securityContext fields: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privileged, capabilities
- hostPID/hostNetwork, allowPrivilegeEscalation
- CI integration and test manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (conceptual)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snospecialsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNoPrivileged
  targets:
  -.target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
```

```yaml
# Falco rule (conceptual)
- rule: ShellOrPtraceInContainer
  condition: container.id != host and evt.type in (execve, ptrace) and proc.pname in ("/bin/sh", "/bin/bash")
  output: "Shell/ptrace detected in container (%container.name)")
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle legitimate privileged tooling in dev/test namespaces?
- How would you minimize false positives in noisy workloads?
- How would you roll out this gate across multiple clusters with different schemas?

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny

  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:

  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: { matchLabels: { app: api } }
    ports:

```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design progressive delivery gates at scale, with multi-cloud constraints and real-world SLO-based rollouts; focuses on policy, tooling (Argo Rollouts, Prometheus), and CI integration; evaluates trade-offs between safety and speed, failure modes; ensures observability and reproducibility.

## Key Concepts

- Progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts Canary
- AnalysisTemplate and Prometheus metrics
- Promotion rules based on consecutive analyses and SLO breach thresholds
- CI gates validating manifest shape and rollout strategy
- Rollback/promotion semantics in production

## Code Example

```yaml
# AnalysisTemplate (Prometheus-based)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-analysis
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    successCondition: result < 0.01
    failureCondition: result >= 0.05
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-operated.default.svc.cluster.local
        query: avg(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

```yaml
# Minimal Rollout using Canary
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/myservice:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-analysis
      stepWeight: 20
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for promotion failure modes if the AnalysisTemplate temporarily becomes unavailable?
- How would you adapt this gate for multi-tenant environments with separate SLIs per tenant?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a reject-by-default policy for hostPath usage, a common attack surface, and to describe how to maintain a dynamic allowlist in production.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- hostPath volumes and host filesystem access risk
- dynamic allowlist via a ConfigMap and a small controller to sync data
- CI validation (dry-run, gatekeeper admissions) and runtime validation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: HostPathPolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: HostPathConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package hostpathpolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i in input.review.object.spec.volumes
        input.review.object.spec.volumes[i].hostPath
        not data.hostpath_allowlist.namespaces[_]
        msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden unless in allowlist"
      }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: HostPathConstraint
metadata:
  name: hostpath-deny
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["v1"]
      kinds: ["Pod"]
```

Compliant manifest (no hostPath):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23
```

Noncompliant manifest (hostPath present):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: data
    hostPath:
      path: /var/lib/data
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /data
      name: data
```

CI/runtime validation plan: run Gatekeeper admission checks on PRs, simulate allowed namespaces via the ConfigMap sync, and perform a runtime audit post-deploy using a test pod to verify policy enforcement.

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

```yaml
name: k8s-security-gate
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          kubectl version --client
          kubeval manifests/*.yaml
          bash scripts/validate.sh
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
violations=0
for f in manifests/*.yaml; do
  if grep -qE "hostPath|runAsNonRoot|NetworkPolicy" "$f"; then :; else echo "General policy missing in $f"; violations=$((violations+1)); fi
  # pseudo-checks for brevity; real checks parse YAML (e.g., yq)
done
if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design scalable, auditable tenant-isolated admission controls that span both manifest validation and runtime enforcement. It also tests knowledge of secret management integration and canary-driven SLO validation patterns.

## Key Concepts

- **Kyverno & OPA Gatekeeper**: Kubernetes admission control frameworks for policy-as-code
- **Namespace RBAC and tenant isolation**: Role-based access control scoped to per-tenant namespaces
- **SecretStore/secretRef**: External secrets management and secure secret injection
- **PodSecurity Standards**: Built-in Kubernetes pod security policies
- **readOnlyRootFilesystem & resource requests/limits**: Container hardening and resource governance
- **Image digests and canary validation**: Supply chain security and progressive delivery validation
- **Kubernetes Audit API**: Compliance logging and incident replay

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: Enforce SecretStore source
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: secrets-from-external-store
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: deny-direct-secret-refs
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      preconditions:
        - selector:
            matchLabels:
              tenant: restricted
      validate:
        message: "Secrets must be sourced from SecretStore, not direct secretRef."
        pattern:
          spec:
            =(containers):
              - =(env):
                  - =(valueFrom):
                      X(secretRef): "*"  # Deny direct secretRef
                      secretStoreRef: "?*"  # Require SecretStore

# OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate: Deny privileged containers
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sPSPPrivilegedContainer
metadata:
  name: no-privileged-containers
spec:
  match:
```

## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint

- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml

apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:

  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Helm templating and basic policy checks in CI for secure defaults, plus ability to craft a simple gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Key Concepts

- Helm templating and values.yaml
- YAML validation with yq
- Kubernetes securityContext basics
- Image tag policy and registry scoping
- CI gate design and test manifests

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/helm-gate.yml
name: Helm gate
on: push
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v1
      - name: Render charts
        run: helm template mychart charts/mychart > /tmp/rendered.yaml
      - name: Validate images
        run: |
          if ! yq e '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[].image' /tmp/rendered.yaml | grep -q registry.example.com/secure/; then echo image origin invalid; exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:latest
          # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# passing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:v1.2.3
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi
```

- How would you extend to multi-container pods?
- How would you adapt for multiple charts in a single repo?
